home.aboutIntro: I did my master's in Information Management at NKUST, and most of my work is in UI/UX design and human factors. As a data analysis intern at e-Excellence, I kept working on how to make the important numbers on a dashboard easy to spot. During an exchange year in Computer Science at THWS in Germany, I saw how differently people read the same button depending on where they grew up. My thesis was on Taiwan's OSCE medical assessment system, where I used user-centered design to rework the back-office workflows from scratch. Drawing the new flow was the easy part. Getting it adopted is harder, and I'm still working on it.
home.aboutResearch: My research keeps returning to one goal: bringing human factors into clinical settings. In 2023 I built an immersive ordering interface for AR glasses, controlled by hand gestures. Later I moved into hospitals, using eye tracking and usability testing to improve a medication recognition system. Across those projects the question has stayed the same: whether an interface can help someone make one fewer mistake when the pressure is high and there's little room for error.
beyondGridParagraphs: When I'm not adjusting pixels or working with data, I'm usually drawing. The two have always overlapped. Halfway through building a web page, a character comes to mind, I can't help drawing it, and it often ends up on that page.

I've been a student ambassador and an international volunteer, and I lived in Würzburg for a while. Living somewhere new meant relearning small things like buying bread or catching a tram, and things I used to take for granted started to need a second look. For a designer, that unfamiliarity is a pretty good deal.

portfolio.eyebrow: Somewhere between technical logic and human intuition.
portfolio.headline: Portfolio
portfolio.intro: I'm more interested in how people use things than in how they look. So I start from evidence: eye tracking, emotional responses and user interviews tell me whether a layout works. Sometimes that means taking a messy technical interface apart and rebuilding it; sometimes it means trying the same dark-mode gray for several nights. Either way, the goal is to find where people get stuck and remove it.

projectQuote.quote: A great interface is like an 8px grid: invisible to the eye, but felt in every seamless interaction.

gallery.headline: Gallery
gallery.intro: I think a good photo has its story before the shutter clicks. I shoot both film and digital: film slows me down, digital lets me take the extra frame. Here you'll find ongoing projects, places I passed along the way, and some everyday shots I barely edited :)

albums.title: Film project

albums.title: Digital Cam project
